relevance_reason: The title reports a de novo SPTAN1 nonsense variant causing hereditary motor neuropathy in a Chinese family, which is the subject of this HMND11 entry. Only the title is available.

findings.statement: Dong et al. (2021) reported a novel de novo nonsense variant in the SPTAN1 gene that caused hereditary motor neuropathy in a Chinese family.
quotes: A novel de novo SPTAN1 nonsense variant causes hereditary motor neuropathy in a Chinese family.

variants.as_reported: novel de novo SPTAN1 nonsense variant

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It reports a de novo SPTAN1 mutation with axonal sensorimotor neuropathy and a developmental disorder. This is a related SPTAN1 neuropathy phenotype that adds to the allelic spectrum of HMND11, but it is not a pure distal motor neuronopathy.

findings.statement: Ylikallio et al. (2020) reported a de novo SPTAN1 mutation associated with axonal sensorimotor neuropathy and a developmental disorder.
quotes: De novo SPTAN1 mutation in axonal sensorimotor neuropathy and developmental disorder.

relevance_reason: This paper first reports heterozygous SPTAN1 nonsense mutations in three families with dominant distal hereditary motor neuropathy, which is the disorder defined by this entry.

findings.statement: In affected members of 3 unrelated families with juvenile-onset autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuropathy, Beijer et al. (2019) used next-generation sequencing to identify heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene, which encodes alpha-II spectrin.
quotes: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families via next-generation sequencing.

findings.statement: Beijer et al. (2019) reported 3 families with juvenile-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy caused by SPTAN1 nonsense mutations. Penetrance was variable in 2 of the 3 families, and the severity of the phenotype differed greatly between patients.
quotes: Variable penetrance was noted for these mutations in two of three families, and phenotype severity differs greatly between patients.

findings.statement: In patient cells, Beijer et al. (2019) found that mutant SPTAN1 mRNA carrying the nonsense mutations was broken down by nonsense-mediated decay and that alpha-II spectrin protein levels were reduced. This contrasts with the dominant-negative SPTAN1 mutations previously described as causing a spectrum of epilepsy phenotypes.
quotes: The mutant mRNA containing nonsense mutations is broken down by nonsense-mediated decay and leads to reduced protein levels in patient cells.
Previously, dominant-negative αII-spectrin gene mutations were described as causal in a spectrum of epilepsy phenotypes.
